Bershad New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. This is the new Jewish cemetery of Bershad, a companion to the old cemetery documented elsewhere in this collection, believed founded in the late 19th century. Bershad's Jewish community, present from the end of the 16th century, became a center of Sabbateanism in the 17th century and Hasidism in the 18th; by 1889, it supported eight synagogues and seven prayer houses. A wartime ghetto absorbed 25,000 Jews expelled from Bukovina and Bessarabia, with mortality reaching 50–70 percent among adults and 80 percent among children; in August 1943, 1,203 Jews mobilized for forced labor in the Nikolaev region never returned. A Jewish underground resistance of 50 people later joined a local partisan unit before liberation. Today the cemetery holds more than 3,000 graves, divided into pre-war and post-war sections separated by roughly five mass graves; an unclaimed ohel from 1906 survives on the grounds, though it is now used as shelter by homeless people, according to the head of the local community.
